key_insight: Selenium alloying and prolonged air annealing suppress residual metallic tellurium in amorphous TeOₓ films, enabling thin-film solar cells with approximately 1.87% peak efficiency.
engineering_relevance: Chemical-state control offers a route to improving oxide-derived photovoltaic absorbers fabricated by vacuum deposition.
method: Thermally evaporate TeO₂:Se powder mixtures containing 90:10 wt%.
Anneal films in air at 225 °C for up to 9 hours.
Integrate the absorber into ITO/ZnO/TeOₓ:Se/MoOₓ/Ag solar cells.
evidence_signal: The optimized 80 nm absorber annealed for 9 hours yielded 0.50 V open-circuit voltage, 8.50 mA/cm² short-circuit current density, a 0.44 fill factor, and photocurrent response from 300–1000 nm.
watch_item: The 9-hour annealing step may constrain manufacturing throughput; long-term device stability is not reported in the abstract.
paper_title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
